# v1.2.0-474: Virtual windows that stay together, and a new version number

A full release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.127`. Five
commits: four virtual window fixes, a feature parked while docking
settles, and a new way of numbering releases.

## Version numbers

- Releases are now `1.2.0-<build>`. The build number is the release's
  commit count, so it only ever goes up and nobody has to pick it. The
  `1.1.0-dev.N` releases keep their names.
- This is a full release, not a pre-release. Installs on any
  `1.1.0-dev` build see it as newer and update as usual.

## Virtual windows

- Clicking one docked window no longer buries the others behind the
  container. The whole group stays above the container, with the window
  you clicked on top.
- The small tab at the top of a container with its title bar hidden is
  the 60 by 18 strip it looks like. It used to be a larger invisible
  window that swallowed clicks meant for the docked window under it.
- Quitting WLM from anywhere other than the tray icon finishes. It used
  to stall after releasing the docked windows, leaving the app half
  closed.
- Deleting a virtual window forgets its saved size and position too.

## Parked for now

- The "when a profile loads" column is gone from the Virtual Windows
  page, and so is what it drove. A Load places the windows that are open
  and reports the rest as missing. It no longer starts a window it can't
  find or opens a fresh copy, and a container closing takes no window
  with it. Your saved choices are kept, and the feature comes back once
  docking is stable.
- The page's column headers and rows now line up.

## Under the hood

- A probe matrix drives every virtual window interaction with one to
  four docked windows, plus a restart pair that closes and reopens the
  app around them. Real apps checked: Calculator, Notepad, Windows
  Terminal, Steam and an Electron app dock and fully dock cleanly. Claude
  Desktop docks as an ordinary window. Its own app layers its window,
  which full dock turns down by design.
